title: The number
summary: A team-mate wants your shirt number. He's worn it since he was nine, everywhere but here, and he offers you his watch for it. A season on, there's a kid in the stand with that number on his back.

ends.title: Gave it up
ends.text: You gave your shirt number to a team-mate who'd worn it since he was nine. He scored more in it than you ever did, and he tells everyone why he has it.

ends.title: Kept it
ends.text: A team-mate wanted your number and you kept it. He wears a different one. He mentions it about once a month.

event.title: The number
event.speaker: mate
setup: {mate.name} catches you by the boot room. He's holding his watch, which is expensive.

say: "Your number. I've worn it since I was nine, everywhere but here. My dad wore it. I'll give you this for it." He holds out the watch.

free.text: He stares at you. Then he hugs you, which he's never done.

watch.text: You've got a very nice watch and a new number. The kit man has to do new shirts and says a word about it.

no.text: "Fair." He takes a number nobody wants. He's fine about it. He says he's fine about it a lot.

beats.title: The watch

event.title: The watch
event.speaker: mate
setup: {mate.name} puts his watch down on the bench next to you. "I said I'd give you this. A deal's a deal."

say: It's his dad's watch. You can see that now.

replies.label: Give it back. "Keep it. It's your dad's."
Keep it. A deal's a deal.
"Lend it me for one game. Then it's yours."

back.text: He holds it for a long time. Then he puts it on.

keep.text: He nods and goes to the gym.

swap.text: You wear it in the car to the game. He laughs at you for wearing a watch to a game.

beats.hint: Your team-mate has brought the watch back

beats.title: On his back

event.title: On his back
event.speaker: mate
setup: A season on. There's a boy in the stand by the tunnel with your old number on his back. {if arc.path=='gave'}It's {mate.short}'s name above it.{/if}{if arc.path=='kept'}It's your name above it.{/if}
{if arc.deep=='back'}He wears his dad's watch on match days. He touches it when he sees you.{/if}
{if arc.deep=='keep'}He hasn't asked for the watch back, and he hasn't forgotten.{/if}

outcomes.text: {mate.short} goes over and gives the boy his armband for the warm-up. "He wore it since he was nine," he tells the boy's dad, pointing at you. "Then I did."
"Your number," {mate.short} says. "Lucky number." He doesn't look at you.
The boy points at {mate.short}, not you. Fair enough.
He waves back, and turns round to show you your name.

beats.hint: A season on, the number in the stand
